prohibitions: Reading metadata beyond file and folder names
guide.summary: Dropbox documents OAuth 2.0 user tokens for each individual account. The requested read-only listing maps to the files.metadata.read scope, and the app must be created with App Folder access so that listing stays inside the app folder. list_folder returns has_more and a cursor, and list_folder/continue pages through the rest, both requiring files.metadata.read. Registration, redirect configuration and the consent step are setup requirements, and the setup is untested. No provider review duration or customer-admin approval step is supplied for this request, and distribution policy for other customer organizations is unresolved.

findings.title: Dropbox documents per-user OAuth 2.0 access tokens for app access to user data
findings.detail: Dropbox states that the API uses OAuth 2.0 so an app accesses a user's data after that user signs in on dropbox.com. The access token is passed as a Bearer token. Apps requesting only User API scopes receive a token associated with the user who authorizes the app.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer account connects its own Dropbox account with OAuth.

evidence.quote: Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0
Overview When working with the Dropbox APIs, your app will access Dropbox on behalf of your users. You’ll need to have each user of your app sign into dropbox.com to
Apps that request only scopes from the User API will receive a token associated with the user that authorizes the app.

findings.title: files.metadata.read grants viewing information about files and folders
findings.detail: files.metadata.read is the scope that lists the file and folder entries. The list_folder and list_folder/continue endpoints both require it. It does not include downloading or writing content, which requires separate scopes.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing file and folder names with list_folder and continuing pages with list_folder/continue.

evidence.quote: Scope Description files.metadata.read View information about files and folders

findings.title: App must be created with App Folder access, which limits file access to one folder
findings.detail: During app creation the developer selects App folder access, which limits the app to a single folder in the user's Dropbox under the /apps folder. This setting is made at app creation and bounds the listing to the app folder.
findings.appliesWhen: The app must be limited to the customer App Folder.

findings.title: Register the app and configure its client credentials and exact redirect URIs before testing
findings.detail: The developer must register the app in the Developer Console to obtain an app key and secret, then register the exact redirect URIs used by the app. Dropbox checks the redirect_uri in the authorization URL against the registered values. Without these, the authorization path cannot be tested.
findings.appliesWhen: Before the first authorization test of the code flow.
